header: 4c's plan for N64Recomp-browser's tools/play_page.mjs, played with its tools/gamepad_probe.js as the preload
(--preload) and --fault reopen: two stand-in pads of one id (Chrome's for an Xbox pad over XInput), plugged in at
the launcher, play a two-player Exhibition race on Kyoto as tools/play_plan_pads.json's four do. In the race each
pad in turn is pulled out and plugged in again (unplugPad, replugPad) at its own place, the other still in, and the
plan prints each player's controller and each controller's player (gGame.playerPad, padPlayer) and the riders'
speeds as each pad alone holds A: each pad still plays its own rider, the first plugged in again below the second of
its model. Both then ride for half a minute and padRumbles() says what reached each pad. Last, it writes the
keyboard's Start bound to P beside Enter to controls.json (the format RecompFrontend saves, only the binding the
player changed). The reopen is the next visit, which runs the start steps again: they press P at the title first,
which does nothing on the first visit, and on the next, where the game has read the file as it started, has to
load: RT64: all [0-9]+ prebuilt shaders built|once the game draws
start: plugPads(["Xbox 360 Controller (XInput STANDARD GAMEPAD)", "Xbox 360 Controller (XInput STANDARD GAMEPAD)"])

window.padA = (i) => { padSet(i, { buttons: { 0: 1 } }); setTimeout(() => padSet(i), 200); return `pad ${i} A`; }; window.allA = async (test, n) => { for (let k = 0; k < 12 && !test(); k++) { for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) padA(i); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1500)); } return test(); }; window.speeds = (n) => { const v = new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(4)); const s = []; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { v.setUint32(0, n64r(0x800E4160 + i * 0x7E0 + 0x420)); s.push(v.getFloat32(0).toFixed(1)); } return s.join(' '); }; 'helpers'
